page: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-4 is a general-purpose server instance belonging to the t2d server family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture. The system is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core testing placing it in the top 25% of evaluated servers. Multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth metrics generally fall within the middle 50% average range, including a large-block read bandwidth of 48.77 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 34.91 GB/sec. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and static web serving throughput are weaker, falling into the bottom 25% of benchmarked systems.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated AMD EPYC core allocation provides predictable compute performance without the resource contention of shared-core models. The 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes this instance suitable for balanced workloads such as general-purpose web serving, software compilation, and moderate database operations. It can also handle lightweight language model inference, processing 135M parameter models at 616.91 tokens per second for prompts and 202.5 tokens per second for text generation.
